questions.question: What capability changes, in present tense, and what must stay byte-identical?
questions.resolution: The store refuses a structurally ill-formed cell identity AT ITS OWN BOUNDARY rather than accepting four loose strings and reaching the six-field validation only after committing to a row set. Everything the fit computes, and all four keystone store invariants, stay identical. H2/H3 are independent hygiene with no runtime coupling to H1.

questions.question: Can the store API be literally typed on CellAddress, as H1's acceptance wording says?
questions.resolution: NO. CellAddress has six fields and addresses ONE cell; the store's unit of work is the k-cell GROUP. class_id is the fan-out axis (absent from the store key) and vocabulary_version is read off the ClassVocabulary argument rather than passed. A CellAddress with a sentinel class_id would violate the value object's own documented invariant. The genuine target is the address PREFIX, which store.py's own prose already calls a 'slot'.
questions.code_evidence: address.py:62-86 (six fields) vs store.py:193-203/255-257/298-300 (five args); store.py:225 loops class_id over vocabulary.class_ids and :233 builds one CellAddress per class; store.py:275 is the read-side mirror; vocabulary_version sourced at store.py:234,:270,:310; the word 'slot' for this exact tuple at store.py:22-23, :186, :301.

questions.question: Given that misfit, what value object does the store API actually take -- (A) a frozen four-field slot with ClassVocabulary still supplying vocabulary_version, (B) the same plus vocabulary_version and a second refusal path, or (C) a per-cell API with the k-fan-out moved to callers?
questions.resolution: (A). A frozen FingerprintSlot(driver, era, channel, what_measure) defined in address.py beside CellAddress, exposing address_for(class_id, vocabulary) -> CellAddress as the sole constructor of a CellAddress on the store path. (C) is rejected because the k-cells-always-populated and no-fit-on-read invariants live IN the fan-out and are #666 Protected Intent. (B) is rejected because vocabulary_version would be asserted twice per call, buying no safety and costing a second refusal path plus its tests.
questions.code_evidence: store.py:14-32 (protected invariants that (C) would destroy); store.py:234 (vocabulary.vocabulary_id already the single authority (B) would duplicate); store.py:22-23 (the inherited 'slot' name).

questions.question: Is scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py the only script in the family missing the worktree-first sys.path guard?

questions.question: Is H3's stated premise true -- are the coverage/summary JSONs already ignored via .agent-work/?
questions.resolution: NO, the premise is false. .gitignore has no `.agent-work/` rule; .agent-work/ is a deliberately TRACKED tree here and the #666 archived artifacts are committed on purpose. The real exposure is (a) three scripts writing regenerable JSON to hardcoded LIVE .agent-work paths with no --out flag, and (b) a higher-value omission the issue's JSON framing missed entirely: the store's own default SQLite DB is not ignored while every sibling own-DB is.
